Items.Authors: Michiel Darcis, Wilbert G. Ras-Vinke, Sebastiaan Y. Haffert, Vincent Chambouleyron, Xavier Le Saux, David S. Doelman, Tonny Coppens, Dimitry Lamers, David Thoen, Matthew A. Kenworthy, Pieter J. de Visser
Items.Title: Multi-wavelength wavefront reconstruction with the Zernike wavefront sensor and MKIDs
Items.Abstract: Future high-contrast imaging instruments require highly precise wavefront sensing. A promising way to improve wavefront sensors is to utilize currently under-exploited wavelength information through new developments such as Microwave Kinetic Inductance Detectors (MKIDs) and semi-analytical gradient descent reconstructors. This work starts with examining the advantages of using multi-wavelength reconstruction for the Zernike Wavefront Sensor (ZWFS). Using numerical simulations, the improvements in dynamic range, photon noise sensitivity and phase unwrapping are investigated. A testbed has been setup to test the multi-wavelength reconstruction together with a 400 pixel MKID. Using a blue and red laser simultaneously, Zernike aberrations are reconstructed using the stream of photon pulses coming from the MKID. These results are compared to those obtained from a CMOS camera with separate blue and red images. The dynamic range extension using multi-wavelength measurements is demonstrated.

Items.Authors: Takeshi Nakazato, Hajime Ezawa, Kanako Sugimoto, Karl Torstensson, Andrés Guzmán, Laura Gómez, Kotomi Taniguchi, Akira Yoshino, Ihor Ihnatiev
Items.Title: New geometrical algorithm for the ALMA single-dish pipeline to identify pointing outlier data and its impact on the ALMA operation
Items.Abstract: The Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) delivers reduced, calibrated, and quality-assessed  data products to its users. In ALMA, the control software excludes data with the pointing direction deviating  from predefined trajectory. However, there are several cases that this mechanism does not work. To overcome  this issue, we developed a generic geometrical algorithm that works without knowing the extent of the observing  region specified by the user. For On-The-Fly raster scan data, median separation of the antenna pointings  from the nominal center of the observation can be used to estimate the size of the observing region even if  outlier data exist. The ALMA Single-Dish Pipeline with the new algorithm excludes pointing outliers from  processing as expected. This improvement significantly reduces the extra effort to reprocess the data with  pointing outliers. The algorithm may have possible applications to other areas requiring outlier detection.

Items.Authors: Simone Lotti, Francesco Monastra, Giacomo Gorla, Matteo D'Andrea, Nicolina Chrysaphi, Monica Laurenza, Claudio Macculi, Luigi Piro
Items.Title: NewAthena X-IFU non-x-ray background: veto optimization and laboratory validation
Items.Abstract: We report on Geant4 simulations of the non–X-ray background (NXB) for the NewAthena X-IFU, focusing on updated mass models, veto strategies, and validation.   The mass model evolved with mission redefinition, including a new cryostat and focal plane assembly, L-grooves, and absorber layouts. High-statistics simulations show modest changes in background relative to the 2017 model, and confirm spatial homogeneity. Although the design is not yet finalized in all its elements, the results’ representativeness increased with respect to previous results.  A sector veto strategy exploiting CryoAC segmentation can keep 75% of the TES array active, raising NXB by ~50%; extending the veto region by Δ pixels reduces the increment to 6% for Δ=5.   A preliminary solar energetic particle simulation confirmed background levels exceeding requirements by three orders of magnitude. Validation against CryoAC prototype data demonstrated strong agreement, supporting the robustness of the simulation framework.

Items.Authors: Katelyn A. Horstman, David Ciardi, Charles Beichman, Jinhao Ge, Stehanie Leifer, Luke Finnerty, Greg Doppmann, Daniel Echeverri, Ben Sappey, Elijah Anakalea-Buckley, Jean-Baptiste Ruffio, Chih-Chun Hsu, Dimitri Mawet, Nemanja Jovanovic
Items.Title: NIR astrocomb integration with Keck Planet Imager and Characterizer (KPIC)
Items.Abstract: Astrocombs are essential calibration tools for spectrographs that specialize in precision and extreme precision radial velocity (PRV/EPRV) measurements to search for planets around stellar hosts. They create a spectrum of discrete and regularly spaced frequencies used to derive wavelength solutions during the data reduction process. Recently, the Keck Planet Imager and Characterizer (KPIC), a fiber injection unit that feeds the high resolution spectrograph NIRSPEC (R~35,000) at Keck Observatory, has successfully integrated a specially built, near-infrared astrocomb into its optical system in H-band (1.5-1.8 microns). We demonstrate that KPIC/NIRSPEC can reach an RV precision low enough to characterize transiting planets orbiting close binary systems. We present the corresponding comb-derived wavelength solution for on-sky observations, together with radial velocities (RVs) of the RV standard star HD 89269 used to evaluate the temporal stability of the wavelength calibration.

Items.Authors: Maria Bergomi, Remon van Gaalen, Carmelo Arcidiacono, Luca Marafatto, Kalyan Radhakrishnan, Gabriele Umbriaco, Paolo Cerpelloni, Thomas M. Herbst, Marco Dima, Davide Greggio, Oleksandra Rebrysh, Silvio Di Rosa, Florian Briegel, Lars Mohr, Jacopo Farinato, Roberto Ragazzoni, Valentina Viotto, Simone Antoniucci, Gianluca Li Causi, Fernando Pedichini, Roberto Piazzesi, Alessio Caratti o Garatti, Al Conrad, Fabrizio Massi, Sam Ragland, Luca Cortese
Items.Title: NirvanaVIS: the visible GLAO-assisted speckle holography imager for LBT approaching first light
Items.Abstract: NirvanaVIS is designed to leverage the wide-field, Ground-Layer Adaptive Optics (GLAO) correction provided by LINC-NIRVANA on the Large Binocular Telescope. Its primary goal is to extend high-resolution imaging into the visible band, retrieving images with a highly uniform PSF across the field.  Implemented on the LN bench, it employs speckle holography to achieve near-diffraction-limited imagery over 52 x 52 arcsec FoV, with a pixel-scale of 6.5 mas/pixel. This yields a spatial resolving power below 20 mas corresponding to a factor of three better than HST and two times better than JWST, enabling diverse science programs.  With the core hardware secured by the end of 2025, if approved for installation, the project is on track to achieve first light in 2027.  This work presents the current status, AIV procedures and commissioning steps. We also detail final solutions for challenges related to the 8K Teledyne COSMOS camera interface to the telescope and the data management strategy.

Items.Authors: Juan Carlos Guerra, Sam Ragland, Brandon Mechtley
Items.Title: Non-invasive optical gain estimation in pyramid wavefront sensors from telemetry using machine learning
Items.Abstract: Modern adaptive optics (AO) instruments at large-aperture observatories require stable loop operation while delivering high correction performance for imaging, spectroscopy, and high-contrast observing modes. The pyra- mid wavefront sensor (PyWFS) is intrinsically nonlinear: its slope response depends on the residual aberration entering the sensor, and therefore changes as atmospheric conditions fluctuate. This sensitivity variation is parameterized by the optical gain, Gopt, defined as the ratio between the WFS command amplitude and the measured sensor response for a test mode.  At the Large Binocular Telescope Observatory (LBTO), the SOUL AO system tracks this nonlinearity by continuously demodulating an 80 Hz sinusoidal probe injected on a controlled mode. The probe provides a direct calibration signal and supports non-common-path-aberration compensation in seeing-tracking operation. However, during rapidly changing seeing it can introduce reactive jumps in the applied correction, an

Items.Authors: Uma Subash, Hanshin Lee
Items.Title: Numerical modeling and performance prediction of the Hobby Eberly Telescope’s new Edge Sensor system
Items.Abstract: The current inductive edge sensor used in the Segment Alignment Maintenance System (SAMS) of the Hobby Eberly Telescope corrects thermally induced misalignments in 91 segments of the primary mirror and maintains it’s sphericity. This old SAMS is getting upgraded to a retroreflector–collimator-based edge sensor. This work presents a numerical model of the new SAMS and its role in dynamic alignment maintenance. The system uses laser distance interferometry to measure changes in channel lengths and estimate segment misalignments, enabling corrections in focus, tip, and tilt. A minimal PID control loop optimizes dynamic alignment control under varying temperature conditions. Case studies using real temperature-time profiles show that the model maintains tip and tilt within 0.07 arcsec 50% of the time and 0.2 arcsec 95% of the time.

Items.Authors: Kyliann Robert, Cyril Petit, Perrine Lognoné, Aurélie Montmerle-Bonnefois, Nicolas Védrenne, Thierry Fusco
Items.Title: Numerical validation of predictive control for PAA precompensation of GEO feeder optical links
Items.Abstract: Going towards predictive AO control for ground-to-GEO optical telecommunication links, we want to make use of the static prediction method presented in Perrine Lognoné's PhD thesis. It uses phase and intensity measurements of the atmospheric turbulence on the downlink path to compute a pre-compensation to apply on the uplink path phase. From this static method, we study the derivation of an LQG-based real-time predictive controller for dynamic correction computation. Will be presented theoretical and numerical aspects, such as the structure of this controller taking phase and intensity as inputs and intensity measurements processing. First end-to-end simulated results are also presented, showcasing performance improvements compared to traditional integrator control using downlink path phase measurements to compute the uplink correction.

Items.Authors: Alejandro Buendía-Roca, Nazim Ali Bharmal, Carlos González-Gutiérrez, Saúl Pérez-Fernández, Juan Antonio de Abol-Blasón, Santiago Iglesias-Álvarez, Julía Fernández Díaz, Fernando Sánchez Lasheras, Francisco Javier de Cos Juez
Items.Title: Off-axis atmospheric turbulence reconstruction with WOMBAT
Items.Abstract: We present a study of off-axis adaptive optics performance using WOMBAT, a system that projects an expanded laser beam through the telescope pupil to sample atmospheric turbulence across multiple directions. Neural networks are trained to reconstruct the three-dimensional turbulence from the beam image. In this work, we quantify how prediction accuracy degrades with increasing angular separation from the telescope axis and identify the main sources of off-axis error. The results outline the practical limits of WOMBAT and the conditions under which neural-network tomography remains reliable for wide-field AO applications.

Items.Authors: Petr Janout, Julienne Böttger, Felipe Pedreros Bustos, Samuel Lévêque, David Jenkins, Deborah Malone, Pierre Haguenauer
Items.Title: On-sky detection of discontinued phase with laser guide star
Items.Abstract: As next-generation large-aperture telescopes adopt segmented primary mirrors, precise co-phasing of segments to well below the observing wavelength is critical for diffraction-limited performance. Residual piston, tip, or tilt between segments introduces phase discontinuities that degrade the point-spread function and overall image quality. We extend previous work on detecting discontinuous optical phase steps and demonstrate on-sky measurement using the CaNaPy facility. CaNaPy, a laser guide star adaptive optics platform for visible wavelengths, enables evaluation under realistic turbulence and adverse conditions. Three precision-fabricated transmissive phase masks simulate segment discontinuities, and the resulting wavefronts are measured with a pyramid piston sensor under various conditions, with and without AO correction. The outcomes of these experiments will inform future on-sky alignment strategies for segmented mirrors.

Items.Authors: Luca Oggioni, Fabrizio Fornasiero, Giorgio M. Pariani, Samuel Ronayette
Items.Title: Optical design and analysis of the InfraRed Telescope (IRT) for the ESA THESEUS mission
Items.Abstract: The InfraRed Telescope (IRT) of the ESA THESEUS mission is a 0.7m off-axis three-mirror anastigmat optimized for imaging and spectroscopy in the 0.7–1.8 µm range to enable rapid GRB follow-up. We present the optical design and performance analysis of the M7 baseline. The system achieves diffraction-limited quality across both photometric and spectroscopic fields, as demonstrated by EE, spot quality and MTF results. A comprehensive Monte-Carlo tolerance analysis, including manufacturing, alignment and stability, defines feasible tolerances and compensator strategies that keep EED50/EED80 within requirements.

Items.Authors: Olivier Lardière, Christian Marois, Adam Johnson, Joeleff Fitzsimmons
Items.Title: Optical design and assembly of CAL2: the NRC Canada facility-class focal plane wavefront sensor for the GPlanetI2 upgrade
Items.Abstract: The Calibration 2 (CAL2) system, being built by NRC-Herzberg with Canadian and international collaborators, is a facility-class focal plane wavefront sensor for the Gemini Planet Imager 2 (GPI2) upgrade, scheduled to be delivered in the Spring of 2026. CAL2 is a complete rebuild of the GPI CAL system. The goal of CAL2 is to replace the dual-arm interferometer by a single-arm all-refractive interferometer, much less sensitive to vibration. CAL2 is based on a self-coherent camera and a Tilt-Gaussian focal plane mask boosting the reference beam and enabling high-speed coherent differential imaging (CDI) and active speckle nulling using GPI deformable mirror. CAL2 should improve GPI contrast by a factor 100 on bright stars. We are presenting here the optical design, the assembly and alignment processes as well as the test results.

Items.Authors: Nicolò Azzaroli, Cédric Plantet, Fernando Quirós-Pacheco, Bo Xin, Arielle Bertrou-Cantou, Gary Muller, Juan Pablo Haddad, Brian McLeod, Jan Kansky, Simone Esposito, Richard Demers
Items.Title: Optical design of the GMT adaptive optics and phasing sensors (GAPS) testbed
Items.Abstract: The Giant Magellan Telescope (GMT) Adaptive Optics and Phasing Sensors (GAPS) testbed is designed to validate key elements of the GMT Natural Guide Star AO control system. This paper presents its optical design. The setup uses a seven-segment mirror to replicate the GMT’s segmented pupil and introduce phasing errors, while a 2k-actuator deformable mirror provides atmospheric turbulence injection, high-order correction, and compensation of minor optical aberrations. The testbed hosts the NGWS prototype, combining a high-order Pyramid WFS with the Hologram Dispersed Fringe Sensor (HDFS), essential for robust measurement of large differential piston between segments. This dual-sensor architecture enables realistic testing and refinement of the GMT NGAO control loop, demonstrating high-order correction and reliable segment phasing.

Items.Authors: Anne-Sophie Poulin-Girard, Nathalie Blanchard, Alexandre Chevrette, Martin Larouche
Items.Title: Optical performance evaluation and end-to-end simulation of a 20cm compact space telescope for precision photometry
Items.Abstract: Precision photometry enables applications such as exoplanet detection, stellar variability studies, asteroid characterization, and space surveillance of Resident Space Objects (RSOs). Space-based instruments provide advantages over ground systems, including continuous observation, improved precision, and access to blocked spectral bands. We present optical performance and task-based simulations for a compact 20 cm VIS-NIR Three-Mirror Anastigmat telescope with a COTS CMOS detector. Metrics such as SNR for faint targets, PSF FWHM variation with object distance, photometric accuracy, and centroid stability are assessed. Monte Carlo tolerancing offers statistical insight into optical performance and supports integration and alignment strategies.

Items.Authors: Salvador Cuevas Cardona, Luis C. Alvarez Nuñez, Rubén Flores-Meza, Beatriz Sánchez , Leonardo Garcés Medina, Oscar Chapa Hernandez, Carolina Keiman, Gerardo Lara Lucario, Carlos Espejo, Nicolas Cardiel, Enol Matilla, Jesús Patron, Alan M. Watson
Items.Title: Optical quality tests in imaging and IFS modes of the GTC/FRIDA instrument in the laboratory
Items.Abstract: We describe the optical quality tests of GTC/FRIDA at the UNAM in Mexico before the GTC engineers’ acceptance in the laboratory. We expect to send FRIDA to La Palma in 2026. FRIDA is an imager and integral field spectrograph (IFS) that will operate in the near-infrared (0.9-2.5m) with the corrected beam provided by GTCAO, the adaptive optics (AO) system of GTC. FRIDA performs the imaging and IFS modes with only an H2RG detector. The instrument provides three pixel/spaxel scales: 10, 20, and 40 mas by means of three cameras. In its IFS mode FRIDA performs a slicer Integral Field Unit with 30 slices and it features two resolutions: (i) medium (R1500-4000) in the z, J ,H, K bands and (ii) high (R30000) in H and K bands. Additionally, FRIDA exhibits high-contrast capabilities with the presence of classical Lyot coronagraphs in both imaging and IFS.

Items.Authors: Akhil Mahesh, Michael D. Audley, Pieter Dieleman, Ilija Lichkovski, Dmitry Orlov, Emilie Kernen, Heino P. Smit, Willem-Jan Vreeling
Items.Title: Optically stimulated luminescence as the origin of the post-pulse tail of the inflight calibration sources for X-IFU
Items.Abstract: Modulated x-ray sources (MXSs) have been used for the in-flight calibration of the Hitomi and XRISM x-ray missions and will be used for NewAthena’s X-IFU. Their principle of operation is the (pulsed) modulation of an LED that stimulates the emission of electrons from the photocathode, which are accelerated by high voltage to the anode target, emitting x-rays. It is known that the MXSs produce a post-pulse decaying tail of x-ray emission of unconfirmed origin, whose intensity decreases relative to the x-ray pulse intensity as the photocathode ages. A lifetime test of an MXS was performed, during which measurements were made that show the tail has a dependence on the wavelength and intensity of the stimulation light, independent of the x-ray pulse intensity. We propose that optically stimulated luminescence in the materials of the MXSs explains the tail’s behaviour.

Items.Authors: Raveena Koliyatan Manamparambil, Nicholas Devaney
Items.Title: Optimizing the performance of holographic wavefront sensor using computer generated holograms
Items.Abstract: This presentation explores how holographic wavefront sensing can improve the performance of adaptive optical systems used in astronomy. We examine how design choices affect measurement accuracy and discuss strategies for optimizing sensor performance.

Items.Authors: Tanmoy Chattopadhyay, Sven Herrmann, Kevan Donlon, Ilya Prigozhin, Peter Orel, Steven W. Allen, Marshall W. Bautz, Michael Cooper, Catherine E. Grant, Beverly LaMarr, Christopher Leitz, Eric D. Miller, R. Glenn Morris, Abigail Y. Pan, Tonya L. Peshel, Artem Poliszczuk, Gregory Prigozhin, Haley R. Stueber, Keith Warner
Items.Title: Output-stage design optimization for high-sensitivity SiSeRO CCDs and SiSeRO active pixel sensors
Items.Abstract: Single electron Sensitive Read Out (SiSeRO) is a new device class for next-generation astronomical X-ray telescopes requiring fast, low-noise, megapixel spectro-imagers and other applications that require sub-electron noise detectors. With the first-generation SiSeRO-CCD prototypes, we achieved a read noise level of around 3.5 electrons in single read mode (625 kpix/sec) and a sub-electron noise performance of 0.51 electrons in Repetitive Non-Destructive Readout mode at an impressive readout speed of 10 kpix/sec. For further maturation of the SiSeRO technology we initiated device simulations of the output stage, in particular, optimization of the sensing transistor and its internal gate geometry to enhance the noise and speed performance. We are also exploring output stage design options to develop a SiSeRO active pixel sensor (APS) matrix. We discuss our device simulation framework and validation using laboratory results from the first-generation SiSeRO devices.

Items.Authors: Nathan K. Long, Barnaby Norris, Daniel S. Dahl, Christopher H. Betters, Julia J. Bryant, Nick Cvetojevic, Sergio Leon-Saval, Frantz Martinache, Marc-Antoine Martinod, Akira Rodziewicz-Ryan, Adam K. Taras, Jin Wei, Peter G. Tuthill
Items.Title: Overcoming the low signal-to-noise problem for hybrid mode-selective photonic lantern-based wavefront correction using machine learning
Items.Abstract: Hybrid mode-selective photonic lanterns transform an input complex point-spread function into several single-mode outputs, where a selected core feeds the fundamental mode to a photonic science instrument, while the remaining cores are used for wavefront sensing in an adaptive optics system. A neural network maps the intensities of the wavefront sensing cores to an estimated wavefront correction, which is applied to an upstream deformable mirror. However, there exists a trade between maximizing the amount of light reserved for the photonic instrument and the reduced signal-to-noise ratios for the wavefront sensing cores. We present a preliminary analysis of this problem using the Seidr instrument, a part of the Asgard Suite for the VLTI. We compare neural network performance, in terms of Strehl ratio, for different wavefront error types, where we show an increase in Strehl Ratio with the use of the hybrid mode-selective photonic lantern wavefront estimation algorithms.

Items.Authors: Ashley D. Baker, Jake Zimmer, Timothee Greffe, Elijah Anakalea-Buckley, Michael Gutierrez, Don Neill, Michael Langmayr, David Hale, Prakriti Gupta, Nemanja Jovanovic, Ricardo Meneses, Robert Bertz, Jean-Baptiste Ruffio, David Brearley, Michael Fitzgerald, Dimitri Mawet, Roger Smith, Reston Nash, Samuel Halverson, Rose Gibson, James Brugger, Jeb Bailey, Hector L. Rodriguez, James Wiley
Items.Title: Overview of the Keck/HISPEC H2RG tracking camera and H4RG-10 detectors​
Items.Abstract: HISPEC is a single-mode fiber-fed, stabilized instrument that will be commissioned on the Keck II telescope in 2027. Its science program will focus on NIR spectral characterization of exoplanets and brown dwarfs with the driving requirement of achieving sub meter per second radial velocity precisions. The two HISPEC spectrometers cover yJ and HK bandpasses respectively, each using an H4RG-10 from the Roman project as its detectors. HISPEC's front-end instrument, which is responsible for coupling light into the science fibers, utilizes a spare JWST H2RG for its tracking camera. The three detectors will be characterized at Caltech before being integrated into the full instrument. Here were provide details on the detector read out electronics, the test plan, the results of the various detector properties measured, and how they relate to the instrument's design and operational requirements as demanded by the HISPEC science program.

Items.Authors: Edvardas Vinerskas, Jalo Nousiainen, Francisco Oyarzun, Mathieu Motte, Angelie Alagao, Vincent Chambouleyron, Romain Fetick, Jonathan Dray, Benoit Neichel, Morgan Gray, Cédric Taïssir Heritier, Jean-François Sauvage, Pierre Jouve, Thierry Fusco
Items.Title: PAPYRUS @ OHP: controlling the second stage with model-based reinforcement learning
Items.Abstract: In this work, we demonstrate a successful on-sky implementation combining a convolutional neural network (CNN) for nonlinear phase reconstruction with a model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL) algorithm for control of the PAPYRUS second-stage adaptive optics system OZIRIIS, which employs the state-of-the-art vector Zernike Wavefront Sensor. The CNN successfully learns the non-linear relationship between the vZWFS signal and the phase, extending the usable sensor range, while the MBRL algorithm compensates for the temporal error. Both algorithms achieve an inference time in the millisecond range, showing an overall improvement over traditional control methods. Hence, this work marks the next step in the control of adaptive optics systems for the purpose of high-contrast direct imaging of exoplanets.

Items.Authors: Francisco Antonio Oyarzun, Benoit Neichel, Thierry Fusco, Cedric-Taissir Heritier, Mathieu Motte, Vincent Chambouleyron, Angelie Alagao
Items.Title: PAPYRUS second stage: non-linear phase reconstruction of the Vector-Zernike wavefront sensor using a convolutional neural network
Items.Abstract: A second stage adaptive optics (AO) system was installed on the PAPYRUS instrument at Observatoire de Haute-Provence. The wavefront sensor of this second stage corresponds to a vector-Zernike (VZ) wavefront sensor (WFS), a highly sensitive but non-linear WFS. Traditional linear reconstruction techniques for the VZ WFS require a high degree of correction from the first stage, and any deviation from that could cause the second stage to diverge. To solve this issue and make the system more robust, we propose to use a convolutional neural network (CNN) as a non-linear phase reconstructor. The CNN can extend the dynamic range of the sensor by using the information scattered through the whole pupil to estimate the phase at each point. To do this, we developed a numerical twin of the second stage, trained the network with the twin, and tested it on the bench yielding better results than the linear reconstructor.

Items.Authors: Jeremy P. Scott, Steve Ertel, Thomas Stuber, Denis Defrère, Romain Laugier
Items.Title: Performance analysis of the Asgard/NOTT nulling interferometer: optimizing observing modes for high-contrast detection
Items.Abstract: This work reports on the simulated performance of the Asgard/NOTT visitor instrument at the VLTI, which uses integrated optics and nulling interferometry to suppress starlight and enable high-contrast detections of exoplanets and hot exozodiacal dust. We compare three distinct observing modes, discussing the trade-offs between each mode in terms of sensitivity, spatial information retention, and complexity. We then introduce the SCIFYsim simulation framework, adapted specifically for NOTT, and present the resulting performance metrics and optimal operational strategies for both exoplanet and hot exozodiacal dust science.

Items.Authors: Shotaro Tada, Kohei Miyakawa, Takehiko Wada, Hirokazu Kataza, Ryouhei Kano, Masanobu Ozaki, Fumihiko Usui, Iona Kondo, Yui Kasagi, Hajime Kawahara, Takayuki Kotani
Items.Title: Performance characterization of an InGaAs NIR sensor for the JASMINE mission
Items.Abstract: JASMINE is a Japanese infrared astrometry mission under study for development toward a 2032 launch, aiming at astrometry of the Galactic center and a planet transit survey around M-dwarfs. Its focal plane will employ four domestically developed ~2k × 2k InGaAs near-infrared detectors. Building on the heritage of the ground-based InGaAs sensor (Nakaya et al. 2016), we are performing upgrades for space use. Low-temperature vacuum tests of a prototype sensor at around 170 K show, based on a nominal conversion gain, a median dark current of 0.70 e-/s/pixel, a median correlated double sampling (CDS) noise of 14.6 e- rms, and a small-scale photoresponse nonuniformity of 0.61% rms in a representative region. A preliminary quantum-efficiency measurement suggests high sensitivity across the JASMINE wavelength range, although the absolute calibration remains under investigation. This presentation reports the current status of the low-temperature detector performance characterization.

Items.Authors: Kenta Sakabe, Kenta Nakamura, Yoshimi Rokugawa, Florian Quatresooz, Hideki Takami, Mareki Honma, Takayuki Usami, Junichi Nakazono, Yuma Abe, Yoshihiko Saito
Items.Title: Performance evaluation of adaptive optics by horizontal-link experiments for ETS-9 optical communications
Items.Abstract: Atmospheric turbulence limits satellite-to-ground free-space optical communication by distorting the wavefront and reducing fiber coupling efficiency. To support NICT's planned 10 Gbps optical communication demonstration using Engineering Test Satellite-9 (ETS-9), we conducted horizontal-path experiments with the NICT Koganei 1 m and 40 cm telescopes. A 1.5 um laser from the 40 cm telescope was received by the AO-equipped 1 m telescope over an 80 m path. Measurements were conducted over six days from November 2025 to March 2026 in daytime and nighttime conditions. The AO loop frequency and gain were varied. The median turbulence parameters were 0.22 m in daytime and 0.20 m at nighttime. The minimum residual wavefront errors were 0.16 um at 2000 Hz and gain 0.3 in daytime, and 0.17 um at 1000 Hz and gain 0.5 at nighttime. AO correction improved the median SMF coupling efficiency by factors of 4.2 and 3.7, respectively.

Items.Authors: Matias Marambio-Jimenez, Yosuke Minowa, Yoshito Ono, Hajime Ogane, Shin Oya, Yusei Koyama, Masayuki Akiyama
Items.Title: Performance of attention-based deep-learning models in Shack-Hartmann wavefront sensor measurements
Items.Abstract: This study evaluates attention-based deep-learning models for wavefront reconstruction in Shack-Hartmann wavefront sensor (SHWFS) systems. Modeled after the Subaru Telescope pupil, 4 datasets of 3.5 million open-loop uncorrelated turbulent phase and image pairs each was simulated across four configurations (8×8 to 32×32 subapertures). A custom Vision Transformer (ViT) with rotary positional embeddings, register tokens, and a cross-attention decoder is benchmarked against a convolutional U-Net and a Maximum A Posteriori (MAP) linear reconstructor. The ViT yields the lowest residual phase variance across all configurations, effectively modeling global spatial correlations and spot-to-spot cross-coupling. While the U-Net captures local features well, it exhibits higher errors on global high-frequency details. This work represents a step toward implementing attention-based models for high-order wavefront sensing in next-generation instrument suites like ULTIMATE-Subaru.

Items.Authors: Anders M. Jorgensen, John Young, Eugene Seneta, David Buscher, Andres Olivares, Juan Paolo Lorenzo Gerardo Barrios, Chris Salcido, James Luis, Emma Floyd
Items.Title: Performance of real-time fringe-tracking software used with FOURIER at MROI
Items.Abstract: We report on the performance of the software fringe-tracking and observing system used with FOURIER. We will present details of the work to optimize the fringe phasor estimation algorithm, and the fringe-tracking performance. We will show results of using the fringe-tracker with data from FOURIER as well as simulated data.

Items.Authors: Grzegorz K. Szymański, P. Wawer, Aleksandra Mirońska, Adam Sikorski, Przemysław Nita, Mateusz Sobiecki, Daniel Półtorak, Konrad R. Skup, Mirosław Rataj
Items.Title: Performance process of FGS subsystem of ARIEL space mission
Items.Abstract: Fine Guiding System (FGS) is a highly advanced optical instrument developed by international Consortium led by CBK PAN in frame of ESA ARIEL space mission. Its goal is to observe atmospheres of exoplanes by providing scientific data using three photometric channels (FGS-1, FGS-2 and VIS-Phot) and one low resolution spectrometer (NIRSpec). To characterize the optical parameters of FGS, an advanced OGSE system was developed and verified at CBK PAN. The main parts of the system include: OGSE ILU which is responsible for providing proper wavelength and power level of light that will illuminate FGS; OGSE OMA which is used for integration and alignment of FGS; OGSE FPM used for detector alignment; OGSE OMC which is responsible for beam forming in TVAC. This paper provides details on design and verification of each major OGSE subsystem.

Items.Authors: Amir E. Bazkiaei, Brent Miszalski, Jesse van de Sande, Nuria P. F. Lorente, Simon O'Toole, Kate Sheng
Items.Title: PERRY: a human-in-the-Loop GUI for precision alignment of MUSE data
Items.Abstract: The Multi Unit Spectroscopic Explorer (MUSE) on the Very Large Telescope produces vast and complex datasets. Misalignments between multiple observations can introduce artifacts that compromise data quality. To address this, we have developed PERRY, a Python-based Graphical User Interface (GUI) for the manual inspection and fine-tuning of MUSE image alignments. Integrated as a quality assurance step within the Pythonic AAO Reduction Environment (PARE), PERRY acts on the outputs of an automated alignment recipe. PERRY provides a suite of interactive tools, including the ability to "blink" between reference and aligned images, dynamic contour overlays, and real-time linear fitting plots. Users can interactively shift and rotate images with user-defined precision, save their adjustments, and continue with the PARE pipeline. We present the architecture of PERRY, demonstrate its key features, and discuss its role in ensuring data quality within a modern astronomical data reduction workflow.

Items.Authors: Ugo Lo Cicero, Philippe Peille, Edoardo Cucchetti, Lionel Jacques, Michela Todaro, Edoardo Alaimo, Luisa Sciortino, Fabio D'Anca, Federico Fiorentino, Marco Barbera
Items.Title: Photon shot-noise analysis for the NewAthena X-IFU reformulation
Items.Abstract: The X-IFU instrument on the NewAthena mission relies on transition edge sensor microcalorimeters operating at millikelvin temperatures. To preserve the detector's high-resolution X-ray spectroscopy, it must be shielded from out-of-band radiation (far-IR to extreme UV) that generates performance-degrading photon shot-noise (PSN). A stack of thermal-optical filters is used to this end. In this paper we describe the critical role of PSN simulations during the instrument reformulation from the original Athena concept to the NewAthena design. The simulations were performed with "ray3cer," a custom ray-tracing software developed to model complex cavity effects and low-transmissivity filters. We show how PSN analysis validated the selection of the filter configuration, key element for ensuring that X-IFU meets its scientific performance requirements.

Items.Authors: Adam K. Taras, Sebastiaan Y. Haffert, Louis Desdoigts
Items.Title: PIAA-ZFWS: a practical and robust wavefront sensor that approaches the fundamental sensitivity limit
Items.Abstract: High-contrast imaging needs extremely sensitive wavefront sensing to correct atmospheric effects. While the limits of the sensitivity of a wavefront sensor are well known, a practical, robust design that saturates these limits remains elusive. This work proposes the PIAA-ZWFS (Phase-Induced Amplitude Apodization-Zernike Wavefront Sensor). We developed a framework to optimize its design, maximizing Fisher information per frame in the presence of both phase and amplitude aberrations. We present optimized designs for various bandwidths, mode bases, and telescope sizes (including ELTs). The PIAA-ZWFS can be optimized for noise (read/photon) or stellar magnitude range. Closed loop simulations show improved performance, nearly saturating the information bound for aberrations with high frequencies and surpassing classic sensors at low frequencies, making it a viable system for future adaptive optics.

Items.Authors: Giacomo Cherchi, Fabrizio Cogato, Natalia Auricchio, Isabella Pagano, Gianalfredo Nicolini, Elisabetta Tommasi, Flavia Calderone, Ann Baeke, Ricardo Bolt, Francesco Borsa, Daniele Brienza, Simonetta Chinellato, Fernando Conde García, Giacomo Dinuzzi, Holger Fischer, Pierre Franco, Nicolas Gorius, Nathalie Gorter, Aline Hermans, Joseph Huesler, Ilina Kondofersky, Lionel Lourit, Demetrio Magrin, Matteo Munari, Amaia Santiago Pe
Items.Title: PLATO camera as-built configuration data list: configuration management and automation with Python tools
Items.Abstract: PLATO is ESA's M3 mission to detect and characterise exoplanets around bright solar-type stars using high-precision space photometry. The payload uses a multi-telescope concept with 26 Cameras (CAMs) produced in series by several institutions. For each CAM, the configuration is reported in an As-Built Configuration Data List (ABCL), which gathers serial numbers, procedures, reports, configuration/calibration files and tracks Non-Conformance Reports (NCRs) and Request for Deviation/Waiver (RFD/W) throughout Assembly, Integration, Testing and Verification (AIT/V) phases. In total, this corresponds to about 1000 items, 1200 documents and over 60 ABCL issues. After introducing the general framework, in this presentation, we present a Python-based workflow, built around a central Excel database and a controlled set of keywords, that automatically generates CAM ABCLs, ensuring consistent as-built data, efficient tracking of NCRs and RFD/W, and a global overview of the PLATO camera population

Items.Authors: Lars Hagge, Markus Garczarczyk, Anja Maaß, Terhi Maibaum, Alexander Steiner
Items.Title: PLM-based digital fabrication planning, control and progress tracking of the CTAO Medium-Sized Telescopes (MSTs)
Items.Abstract: The CTAO plans to build nine Medium-Sized Telescopes (MST) at its Northern site in La Palma (Canaries, Spain), and fourteen at its Southern site in Paranal (Chile). Two pathfinder telescopes are currently being fabricated for the Southern site. A key objective of the pathfinders is to prepare for subsequent series production. For this, the entire fabrication process is digitalized based on a PLM system, which serves as a central collaboration platform and supports the management of a widely distributed manufacturing workflow. The presentation outlines the fabrication process and its challenges, introduces the digitalized fabrication control solution, and summarizes the current status, experience gained, and lessons learned.

Items.Authors: Ioannis Apergis, Daniel Bayliss, Paul Chote, James McCormac, Peter J. Wheatley, Edward M. Bryant, Jorge Fernández Fernández, Sam Gill, Leonidas Asimakoulas
Items.Title: Precise photometry with a fast readout scientific CMOS camera
Items.Abstract: Scientific CMOS cameras provide fast readout speeds and low read noise, offering clear advantages over traditional CCD detectors. In this work, we assess the performance of the Marana CMOS camera through simultaneous photometric observations of eight transiting exoplanets, taken alongside a CCD camera at the Next Generation Transit Survey (NGTS) facility at Paranal Observatory in Chile. The CMOS camera delivers white-noise dominated photometry, achieving ~500 ppm on 30-minute timescales, comparable to the CCD. Its significantly faster readout enables a ~20% increase in collected photons per duty cycle. These results demonstrate that modern CMOS detectors are well suited for high-precision, time-domain astronomical observations.

Items.Authors: Guido Torrioli, Paolo Bastia, Giovanni Benevento, Fabio Chiarello, Artur Coimbra, Matteo D'Andrea, Luca Giganti, Giacomo Gorla, Claudio Macculi, Luigi Piro, Francesco Villa
Items.Title: Preliminary characterization of the cryogenic anticoincidence detector (CryoAC) warm electronics breadboard for the X-IFU NewAthena instrument
Items.Abstract: NewAthena is ESA's next-generation X-ray observatory. Its X-ray Integral Field Unit (X-IFU) is a cryogenic TES imaging spectrometer operating at 50 mK. To achieve the required background performance, X-IFU incorporates a Cryogenic AntiCoincidence detector (CryoAC), which identifies and rejects particle-induced events. The CryoAC consists of four TES-based pixels read out by SQUIDs operated in Flux Locked Loop configuration. Its warm electronics comprises the analog Warm Front-End Electronics (WFEE), implementing the FLL, and the Warm Back-End Electronics (WBEE), responsible for signal digitization, event processing, and communication with the Instrument Control Unit (ICU). This work presents the implementation and preliminary characterization of the CryoAC warm electronics breadboards, including operation with the CryoAC Demonstration Model and investigations of alternative grounding schemes.

Items.Authors: Dehbia Lattab, Diego Götz, Eric Doumayrou, Aline Meuris, Frédéric Pinsard, Thibault Pichon, Marin Prieur, Samuel Ronayette, Thierry Tourrette, François Visticot, Ludovic Genolet, Enrico Bozzo, Andras Peter Joo, Bendegúz Koncz, Rebeka Kiss, Viktor L. Toth, Henri Triou, Mickaël Lacroix
Items.Title: Preliminary design of the camera of the InfraRed Telescope of the THESEUS astronomy mission
Items.Abstract: The instrument InfraRed Telescope (IRT) of the THESEUS mission is composed of an Optical System and an Instrument Control System. The former includes the Telescope and the Camera subsystems. The Camera is mainly composed of a filter wheel, a focal plane and a calibration unit. It provides photometry in five bands in the 0.7 to 1.8 µm wavelength range as well as spectroscopy capability (0.8-1.6 µm) with a grating prism for the brightest sources. Coupled to a dedicated scientific on-board software, the camera images are used to identify and localise the transient sources with a 5 arcsec precision. A photo-Z imaging technique is also applied on-board to estimate the redshift with 10% precision. The paper presents the technical choices done to propose a camera design compliant with the instrument performance, optimising the system resources and the technology maturity. The camera structure was breadboarded to demonstrate the appropriate thermoelastic behaviour of the proposed solution.

Items.Authors: Isabel J. Kain, Renate Kupke, Daren Dillon, R. Deno Stelter, Rosalie McGurk, Gwendolin Weber-Stover, Athira Unni, Marc Kassis, Scott Lilley, Peyton Benac, Mackenzie Lach, Arun Surya, Amirul Hasan, Ravinder Banyal, Raquel Martinez, Nicholas MacDonald, William Deich, Aaron Hunter, Emily Plume, Michael Gonzales, Cristian Rodriguez, Arjun Kumar, Cyril Bourgenot, Paul White, Jürgen Schmoll, James T. Wells, Spencer Davies, David Bramall, Dimitri Mawet, Olivier Absil, Michael Fitzgerald, Eric Wang, Steph Sallum, Andy Skemer
Items.Title: Pre-ship optical verification of the SCALES instrument for Keck Observatory
Items.Abstract: The Slicer Combined with an Array of Lenslets for Exoplanet Spectroscopy (SCALES) instrument is a 1-5µm imager and 2-5µm integral field spectrograph, soon to be commissioned on the Keck II Telescope in Fall 2026. SCALES is optimized for exoplanet high-contrast imaging and spectroscopic characterization, and will be sensitive to older, colder exoplanets than existing instrumentation. The 12.3”x 12.3” imaging channel is designed to replicate the capabilities of NIRC2, and the low (R∼35-250, 2.2”x2.2” FOV) and medium (R∼3500-7000, 0.36”x0.34” FOV) spectral resolution modes offer new capabilities compared to existing Keck instrumentation. We present preliminary optical performance results from pre-ship laboratory testing of SCALES.

Items.Authors: Desirée Della Monica Ferreira, Alessandro Morello, David Blanquez, Denis Tcherniak, Søren Møller, Gabriel Tello, Guillermo Bravo Guinea, Søren Møller Pedersen
Items.Title: Product and quality assurance strategies for space instrumentation development: from power electronics to structural qualification
Items.Abstract: This paper will present the Product and Quality Assurance activities being implemented at DTU Space during the development of the LISA Power Supply Module and the ARIEL bipods structures. PA/QA processes are essential for ensuring mission reliability, traceability, quality and compliance with mission requirements and applicable standards such as ECSS, ISO 9001. The contribution presents how these procedures are applied to our contributions. For the LISA PSM, PA/QA activities focus on the development of the PSM, including parts screening and procurement, and qualification testing to ensure compliance under operational conditions over the mission lifetime. On the other hand, the role in the ARIEL mission relates to the mechanical integrity of bipods through the qualification of CFRP struts, supported by material characterization, process control, and structural verification. Together, these projects highlights how systematic PA/QA approaches are essential to mitigate technical risks.

Items.Authors: Rainer Köhler, Robert Ligon, Karolina Kubiak, Narsireddy Anugu, Christopher Farrington, Douglas R. Gies, Cyprien Lanthermann, Gail Schaefer, Nic Scott, Nils Turner
Items.Title: Progress on integrating the mobile telescope into the CHARA array
Items.Abstract: The CHARA Array consists of 6 telescopes at fixed positions, connected by vacuum pipes to the central beam combiner.  The CHARA Michelson Array Pathfinder (CMAP) project includes two major components: 1) a mobile telescope that can be placed at a number of locations, and 2) a fiber optic relay system to transport light to the existing delay lines and beam combiners.  The mobile telescope is a 1m Ritchey-Chrétien system built by PlaneWave Instruments, equipped with a custom-built instrument bench with Adaptive Optics and fiber injection.  It is mounted in a custom enclosure on a trailer that can be moved around Mount Wilson Observatory.  In this contribution, we present the progress on the various subsystems needed to integrate the new telescope and beam transport method into the existing CHARA hardware and software environment.

Items.Authors: Isabel J. Kain, John O'Meara, Marc Kassis, Antonin Bouchez, Peter Wizinowich, James Lyke, Avinash Surendran, Imke de Pater, Katherine de Kleer, Ned Molter, Steph Sallum, Rosalie McGurk, Andy Skemer
Items.Title: Progress on twilight observing with SCALES on Keck
Items.Abstract: Twilight presents an opportunity for infrared astronomers: while the brightening sky closes the observing window for optical astronomers, the infrared sky does not significantly brighten even through sunrise. The Slicer Combined with an Array of Lenslets for Exoplanet Spectroscopy (SCALES) instrument is a 1-5µm imager and 2-5µm integral field spectrograph currently being commissioned at Keck Observatory, which will execute a twilight science program that expands on the successes of the extant Twilight Zone program with NIRC2 and OSIRIS. This paper presents an optimized and executable SCALES twilight program, prioritizing (1) monitoring of Solar System objects to study time-domain phenomena and support future NASA missions, and (2) support transiting exoplanet discovery by conducting direct imaging follow-up of TESS Objects of Interest (TOIs). We describe the science program along with optimized observing configurations and report preliminary results from SCALES commissioning.

Items.Authors: Josh Walawender, Andrew Howard, Sam Halverson, Jeff Mader, Tyler Coda, Erik Petigura, Jack Lubin, Grant M. Hill, John Valliant
Items.Title: Progress toward stable operations of the Keck Planet Finder
Items.Abstract: The Keck Planet Finder is a precision radial velocity, fiber fed, high resolution visible light spectrograph which was commissioned at the W. M. Keck Observatory in 2022. Since then, it has undergone 4 servicing missions. Some of the scientific goals of the instrument, however, require long term instrumental stability. Each servicing mission has affected observational programs which span the time across servicing missions. We present a summary of the operational challenges the work was designed to mitigate and the observatory's operational plan for achieving the decade long operational stability required by KPF's science goals.    Furthermore, achieving those long term science goals requires updates to the observatory's operational model. The cadenced observations which yield the best science are poor fit to a classically scheduled observatory. We will also present our scheme for KPF queue operations within a classically scheduled operational environment.

Items.Authors: E. Ligon, K. Kubiak, R. Köhler, N. Anugu, T. ten Brummelaar, V. Castillo, C. Farrington, B. Flores, L. Grossard, C. Lanthermann, O. Majoinen, H. Renteria, F. Reynaud, S. Ridgway, G. Schaefer, N. Scott, N. Turner, N. Vargas, C. Woods, D. Gies
Items.Title: Progress towards CMAP first on-sky fringes
Items.Abstract: The Center for High Angular Resolution Astronomy (CHARA) Array currently consists of 6 telescopes at fixed positions, connected by vacuum pipes to the delay lines. The CHARA Michelson Array Pathfinder (CMAP) project includes two major components: 1) a mobile telescope that can be placed at a number of locations, and 2) a fiber optic relay system to transport light to the beam combining facility. We present our first on-sky fringes and the work done to reach this result.

Items.Authors: Vincenzo Cianniello, Christian Eredia, Enrico Cascone, Paolo Saracco, Emilio Molinari
Items.Title: Project management in support of an innovative engineering approach: the challenge of designing next-generation astronomical instrumentation
Items.Abstract: Designing next-generation astronomical infrastructures, such as large telescopes and advanced observational instruments, requires an integrated and systematic project management approach. These projects involve high technical complexity, interdependent mechanical, optical, and electronic systems, tight budgets, and schedules linked to multiple stakeholders, while demanding rigorous quality and safety standards.  Structured project management enables effective planning, monitoring, and control across the entire project lifecycle, from concept and preliminary design to construction, integration, testing, and commissioning. Strategic planning, cost and schedule control, knowledge management, and stakeholder communication are thus essential to transform innovative concepts into operational instruments, opening new window on the universe and positioning project management as a key enabler of engineering innovation in modern astronomy.

Items.Authors: Daniel Harbeck, Curtis McCully, Matthew Daily, Prerana Kottapali
Items.Title: Propagating random telegraph noise in Las Cumbres Observatory’s CMOS data
Items.Abstract: At Las Cumbres Observatory we introduced CMOS-based imagers (QHY600 with Sony IMX455 sensors) as  the main cameras in our global network of ten 35-cm telescopes. The deployment of CMOS detectors in the small telescope network also serves as a pathfinder for a possible future. We report some of the first lessons learned from using CMOS cameras in a professional astronomy production environment. In particular, we focus on characterizing and treating random telegraph signal (RTS), an additional noise component in CMOS cameras. We have developed procedures to model RTS and then seed and propagate a simplified per-pixel noise model in our data processing pipeline BANZAI. We are exploring more advanced mitigation studies, such as using model such as using modeled multi-modal RTS distributions as a prior for maximum likelihood fitting when stacking images, which is capable of estimating a pixel’s true readout value with smaller samples than simple averaging.

Items.Authors: Kathryn Barrett, Ollie J. D. Farley, David Jenkins, Noelia Martinez Rey, Bernadett Stadler, Domenico Bonaccini-Calia, James Osborn
Items.Title: Propagation delay results for measuring tip-tilt for GEO uplink pre-compensation
Items.Abstract: We present successful numerical simulation results for uplink tilt pre-compensation for optical feeder links in ground-to-satellite optical communications. It is vital to pre-compensate the uplink beam at the point-ahead angle to ensure the stability of the link. A laser guide star (LGS) can measure the higher order modes at the point-ahead angle, giving an improvement in the data throughput, but with its inability to directly measure the tip and tilt modes, the optical link will still suffer frequent fades. We have developed the propagation delay method to be applied for optical communications. It is a technique to indirectly measure the tip and tilt from a sodium LGS, allowing for uplink tilt pre-compensation. Our numerical simulations show improvement in comparison to tilt pre-compensation using only the downlink tilt of the satellite. We intend to also explore how this method could be used to increase sky coverage for adaptive optics in astronomy.

Items.Authors: Eemil Halonen, Jalo Nousiainen, Markus Kasper, Nuutti Hyvönen
Items.Title: Pseudo closed-loop bootstrapping for reinforcement learning-based AO control
Items.Abstract: Direct imaging of Earth-like exoplanets around nearby stars requires extreme AO (XAO) that delivers high contrast at very small angles. Performance is limited by fast XAO residuals and quasi-static speckles, requiring ultra-sensitive yet highly nonlinear wavefront sensors. Greater sensitivity amplifies the response to critical aberrations, such as low-wind-effect petal modes, but severely challenges conventional linear reconstructors. Reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as a powerful XAO control tool, with model-based RL variants already reducing latency, misregistration, and moderate nonlinearities. We propose a robust learning strategy in which original PO4AO or a pixel-based variant (PiPO4AO) is pre-calibrated using an internal light source and a DM mirror, enabling direct on-sky closed-loop operation without a stable integrator controller.

Items.Authors: Lukas Stock, Andreas Schrimpf
Items.Title: PSF modeling for inexpensive oﬀ-the-shelf echelle spectrographs
Items.Abstract: Various spectroscopic target systems, such as close binary stars, require a very high cadence in the range of minutes to hours in order to determine their orbits using the radial velocity method. Due to limited observation time, this high cadence cannot be achieved by high-resolution spectrographs. However, for bright target systems (approx. Vmag <= 10), off-the-shelf echelle spectrographs on small telescopes (diameter <= 50 cm) can perform this task.  Due to their comparatively low price such instruments exhibit optical imperfections that limit the effective resolution of the instrument. Thus, ThAr calibration lines are distorted on the camera chip. I will present a way to increase the resolution through PSF modeling of these emission lines in the extraction software. This new extraction method is part of a new, open-source data reduction software written in Python 3 called PyVesta, which will be released shortly.

Items.Authors: Martin M. Roth, Paško Roje, Stella Vješnica, Stefan Cikota, Alex J. Brown, Mike Kretlow, Marco Azzaro, Santiago Reinhart, Jesús Aceituno, Thomas Kupfer
Items.Title: qCMOS on sky: commissioning of the ORCA-TWIN project
Items.Abstract: Quanta image sensors have attracted attention for their unique capabilities for time domain astronomy and other applications requiring photon counting with high quantum efficiency and a large dynamic range, combined with very low noise and fast readout. The Hamamatsu ORCA-Quest 2 model C15550-22UP is an off-the-shelf camera delivering such capabilities. ORCA-TWIN is a fast track project of the emerging German Center for Astrophysics (DZA) that aspires to implement simultaneous observation at fast cadence from 1m class telescopes at two sites with a baseline of 1800 km, the Calar Alto and Teide observatories. We present the scientific rationale for LEOs, NEO and other solar system objects, as well as time domain astronomy, and first results form commissioning at Calar Alto.

Items.Authors: Valentin Emberger, Luisa Ostler, Johannes Müller-Seidlitz, Wolfgang Treberer-Treberspurg, Astrid Mayr, Robert Andritschke, Annika Behrens, Günter Hauser, Peter Lechner, Leonie Sommer
Items.Title: Radiation effects and noise evolution in NewAthena WFI flight-production sensors
Items.Abstract: The Wide Field Imager (WFI), one of the two instruments aboard ESA’s upcoming large-class   X-ray observatory NewAthena, is optimized for imaging spectroscopy in the 0.2–15 keV energy range. Its focal plane comprises back-illuminated DEPFET sensors designed for high radiation tolerance. As part of the flight-production qualification, sensors were characterized to assess performance degradation induced by ionizing and non-ionizing radiation. The devices were irradiated with 62.4 MeV protons and 17.4 keV X-rays to total doses of   2.6E9 10-MeV-protons/cm² and 1.5 krad, respectively. We present the resulting changes in readout noise, dark current, and threshold voltage and compare them with the outcomes of a previous irradiation campaign on pre-flight devices. Implications for the required operating temperature and the expected end-of-life performance of the instrument are discussed.

Items.Authors: Fatima De Frondat Laadim, Julien Cailleux, Assia El Mouden, Nicola La Palombara, Jean-Laurent Dournaux, Giuseppe Leto, Cesare Molfese, Alessio Trois, Gianpiero Tagliaferri, Philippe Laporte, Hélène Sol, Andréas Zech, Alida Marchetti, Gianluca Giavitto, Richard White, Valentina Giordano, Fulvio Gianotti, Laura Proserpio, Giorgia Sironi, Gino Tosti, Ismam Abu, Claudio Arena, Carmelo Gargano, Pietro Giuseppe Bruno, William WANG, Salvatore Scuderi, Akira Okumura, James Anthony Hinton, Giovanni Pareschi, Christian Scaramozza, Simone Piras, Luca Trevisan, Alonda Sola-Molina, Connor Duffyk, Federico Russol Russol, Giovanni Lombardi, Laura Sarchi, Luigi Lessio, Primo Attinà, Rachele Millule, Samuel Branger, Simone Iovenittie, Valerio Pastorel, Vito Confortil
Items.Title: RAMS analysis of small-sized telescopes (SST) for CTAO
Items.Abstract: The Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO) will be the world’s largest and most sensitive ground-based gamma-ray telescope array, with sites in La Palma, Spain, and the Atacama Desert, Chile. Its goal is to study high-energy cosmic phenomena such as black holes, pulsars, and supernova remnants by detecting Cherenkov radiation produced when gamma rays interact with the atmosphere. The Small-sized Telescopes (SST) will focus on the highest energy range.    Given CTAO’s 30-year lifetime and the harsh desert environment, the project demands exceptional Reliability, Availability, Maintainability, and Safety (RAMS), aiming for 98.5% telescope availability. This paper presents the SST RAMS analysis, detailing the methodology, tools, and maintenance strategies developed collaboratively to ensure high performance, minimize downtime, and meet stringent operational and cost requirements.
